articles.title: Mint Explainer: Will Sebi’s new rules on currency derivatives help the falling rupee?
articles.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has tightened rules on currency derivatives trading to protect the rupee from volatility.
articles.explain: Derivatives are contracts whose value is based on the price of something else, like the exchange rate between the rupee and the dollar. By limiting 'unhedged' positions, regulators are forcing traders to prove they have a real reason to buy these contracts, rather than just speculating. This helps prevent traders from overwhelming the market and causing the rupee's value to crash unnecessarily.

story.title: SEBI Currency Derivative Regulation
story.so_far: The rupee is a major currency monitored by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and SEBI. Speculative trading, where participants bet on price movements without holding an underlying asset (unhedged), can create artificial downward pressure on the currency's value during volatile times.
